definitions.approval: When did a city body most recently approve this project? Counts: SFMTA Board of Directors approval or legislation, adoption of a plan, the City Traffic Engineer's approval, a timeline stage named Project Approvals, Legislation or Plan Adoption (pick the last date of its range), including planned dates. Does not count: environmental review, or approval of a different project.
definitions.construction_end: When does construction or implementation of this project finish or when did it finish? Counts: the last date of a Construction or Implementation stage's range, 'construction complete', 'substantially complete', 'implementation was completed', a 'Project Completion' stage, and a 'Predicted Completion' field, whatever phase the project is in, since it is the best date the page gives. Does not count: close-out, evaluation, the end of a planning, design, outreach or approval stage, or the completion of housing or another project. A building's opening, reopening or reoccupation ('opened on', 'reactivated') is its construction end. If the project has several phases, the end of the latest phase counts. If the page describes a pilot, trial or interim installation and names a later build of this project that replaced or will replace it, the pilot's dates do not count; use the later build's.
definitions.construction_start: When does construction or implementation of this project begin or when did it begin? Counts: 'construction begins/began/starts', a timeline stage named Construction, Implementation, Installation or Near-term Implementation (use the first date of its range). Does not count: design, outreach, environmental review, approval or completion dates, or another project's or program's work. If the project has several phases, the start of the earliest phase counts. If the page revises an estimate, only the revised estimate counts. A sentence saying work was completed, finished or substantially implemented by a date ("As of Fall 2022, the design was substantially implemented", "the first phase was completed in August 2017") gives an end date, not this one. An earlier interim version of the same street or corridor (a COVID-19 response Slow Street) is this project, and its installation date counts unless the page names a later build that replaced it. If the page describes a pilot, trial or interim installation and names a later build of this project that replaced or will replace it, the pilot's dates do not count; use the later build's.
definitions.consultation: When was the most recent public consultation for this project? Counts: open houses, virtual open houses, community meetings, workshops, surveys, door-to-door outreach, tabling, office hours, and timeline stages named outreach or community engagement (pick the last date of such a stage's range). Does not count: an engineering public hearing, a Board of Directors meeting, or outreach for a different project. A sentence saying work was completed, finished or substantially implemented by a date ("As of Fall 2022, the design was substantially implemented", "the first phase was completed in August 2017") gives an end date, not this one.
definitions.hearing: When was the most recent SFMTA public hearing on this project? Counts: an engineering public hearing, a public hearing notice for this project, or a timeline stage named public hearing. Does not count: a Board of Directors meeting or an open house.
